en: Taal Volcano's main crater contains a lake where a small volcanic island periodically emerges from the water.
The Pagsanjan River in Laguna is observable as a waterway flowing through deep, narrow gorges with steep rapids.
The Rafflesia plant in Luzon's rainforests produces the largest individual flower on Earth, reaching three feet wide.
The white sand on Boracay Island's beaches is visibly composed of crushed coral and tiny foraminifera shells.
The southwest monsoon, or habagat, brings observable dark rain clouds and strong winds to the western Philippines.
Laguna de Bay is observable as a massive, shallow lake bordered by the provinces of Rizal and Laguna.
Mount Pulag, Luzon's highest peak, is frequently covered by a thick, observable sea of clouds at dawn.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan is observable as an underground river flowing through a cave into the sea.
The Philippine eagle has a distinct, observable crest of long, shaggy feathers covering its head and neck.
The Tubbataha Reefs in the Sulu Sea contain highly visible, colorful coral atolls teeming with diverse marine life.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over a thousand cone-shaped limestone hills that turn brown during summer.
The Banaue Rice Terraces feature observable, ancient stone walls carved directly into the natural contours of mountain slopes.
